newsitem.title: UK: Bristol-Myers acquires rights to Novartis AIDS drugs.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers acquires rights to Novartis AIDS drugs.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. said Tuesday it acquired worldwide development and marketing rights for two protease inhibitors from Novartis Pharma AG.
Bristol said it would start Phase II clinical trials on one of the drugs, known as BMS-234475 (formerly CGP-61755).

Protease inhibitors are the second line of attack against HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, after nucleotide-analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitors such as Glaxo's AZT and Bristol's Videx or ddI. When three drugs, including a protease inhibitor, are combined, the treatment can suppress HIV to undetectable levels.
Each HIV drug affects a slightly different point in HIV's replicative cycle. Protease inhibitors interfere with production of an enzyme that helps formulate the virus' structural proteins.
But the virus can quickly mutate to become resistant to various drugs -- so doctors are keen to have a number of different drugs to choose from in each category.

The peptidomimetic protease inhibitor acquired by Bristol-Myers is in the same class as the other protease inhibitors on the market -- Roche's saquinavir, Merck's indinavir, Abbott's ritonavir and Agouron's nelfinavir.

"Bristol-Myers Squibb also will continue preclinical work to evaluate BMS-232623 (CGP-73547), a potent azapeptide inhibitor of HIV protease now in the early stages of preclinical development," the statement said.

"While more study is needed before we can determine the true utility of the new compounds, we're pleased to investigate the role of these new protease inhibitors, focusing on their use in combination therapy with other antiretroviral drugs," said Sol Rajfer, senior vice president for clinical research for Bristol.
